_source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing fetched 2026-09-06, the five older models added from a fresh fetch of the same page on 2026-09-23 (issue #63); USD per million tokens; cache_write is the 5-minute rate. meter_weight is meter percent per list dollar relative to Sonnet 5; Fable's 1.0 is measured: the 2026-09-06 5-tick Fable probe cost $1.08 of list value per 1% against $0.98 for Sonnet on the same cache-write-heavy payload (ratio 0.91, within probe error). class_weight is meter percent per list dollar for each token class relative to cache_write, the class the Sonnet probe is made of. class_weight.output is maintained by the publisher (tracker/weight.py): the weekly Sunday Fable output run (bin/output-probe.sh, payload output) supplies a row, and the next daily publish solves the weight at which that row and the latest Fable prose row read the same meter dollars per 1%, writes it to every model here, and records the pair under _output_weight; a value more than 30% from the current one is refused, recorded with applied false, and alerts Jonathan instead. The 1.8 hand-entered on 2026-09-06 was the crude ratio of the two rows' list values; the first automatic recompute from the same pair gave 1.95 because the output row's own cache traffic (12% of its list value) sits on the unweighted side. input and cache_read are unmeasured and assumed 1.0; the same class weights are assumed for every model. Opus 5's 1.0 is measured too: a paired run on the Jono Work account on 2026-09-08, same 5-hour window, cost $0.918 of list value per 1% for Opus (ticks 7 to 10) against $0.963 for Sonnet (ticks 2 to 5), ratio 0.954, within probe error, so Opus keeps meter_weight 1.0. The first Opus row (2026-09-07 on Dave, $0.682 per 1%, early tick) is flagged outlier by hand under the rotation's own decide rule: the later same-model reading agreed with the all-model median, not with it. cache_read is 0.0 since 2026-09-16, measured on masterrig: over 111 idle-bounded windows (tools/idle_burst.py, 18 Aug to 15 Sep, $4,759 of list value against 2,214 meter points) the list value per 1% climbs with the cache_read share of the window (median $1.67 at a 25-45% share, $2.69 at 45-60%, $3.28 at 60-75%, $6.13 above 75%) while the non-cache_read value per 1% holds at $1.11, $1.15, $1.25, $1.43 across the same bins ($0.94 aggregate), and a non-negative least squares fit gives cache_read a weight of 0.000 in every configuration tried. The probe never saw this because its payload is 98% cache_write by list value. output is 1.0 since 2026-09-16, measured on gs: a least-squares fit of meter movement on list dollars of (input + cache_write) and of output over the 60 jwork stretches the capture check accepted 2026-09-05..15 (tracker.gs_passive --fit-output-weight, cache_read pinned at 0.0) gives output 1.018 relative to cache_write, residual 1.7 points of meter on 10% stretches, with output 42% of the list value fitted. The 1.8 from the single 2026-09-06 output probe run is superseded; the Sunday output probe is retired with the rest of the probes. The five older models. Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 were unpriced until 2026-09-23 and every stretch containing one of their tokens was thrown away whole (tracker/gs_passive.py publishable, audit finding 9): 167 of masterrig's 251 stretches, 33 of jwork's 140 and 22 of dave's 52. Each of the five has its own row on the pricing page and its prices are taken from it verbatim -- Opus 4.8 and Opus 4.7 at $5/$6.25/$10/$0.50/$25, identical to Opus 5; Opus 5.5 at $4/$5/$8/$0.20/$20; Sonnet 4.6 at $3/$3.75/$6/$0.30/$15; Haiku 4.5 at $1/$1.25/$2/$0.10/$5 (input, 5m cache write, 1h cache write, cache read, output). Nothing here is filled from memory: `<synthetic>` has no row on the page and stays unpriced, which costs nothing because every `<synthetic>` turn carries zero tokens (117 turns, 0 tokens, on masterrig 2026-08-20..09-23). Their meter_weight is 1.0 and is ASSUMED, not measured. The measurement was attempted and failed: masterrig's idle-bounded windows (tools/idle_burst.py, all history, cache_read at 0) hold no window at all that is 60% or more Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 or Opus 5.5, one that is Opus 4.8 ($1.72 per 1%, against Opus 5's $1.73 median over n=37) and two that are Opus 4.7 ($0.28 and $0.39, both on 29-30 August, a stretch where every model reads low because the meter moved on work this host's transcripts never saw). A non-negative least squares fit of meter movement on per-model list dollars over all 135 windows gives these five 0.05% to 1.0% of the list value and coefficients that pin at zero or blow up (Haiku 52.4 percent per dollar before 14 September, 0.0 after), so it measures nothing about them. 1.0 is therefore the same unadjusted treatment the three current rows already have, and it is not a claim that the meter charges these models in proportion to their list price. The alternative, if the meter charges one credit rate per family whatever the version -- which is what the _credits table below assumes and what the family keying of `matches` exists for -- would be meter_weight 1/1.5 for Sonnet 4.6, 1/0.8 for Opus 5.5 and about 2/3 for Haiku 4.5 (its reference rate is a third of Sonnet's against half the list price), and 1.0 for both Opus 4.7 and 4.8, whose list prices equal Opus 5's so the question does not arise. It is not applied because meter_weight is not where this repository reconciles credits with list dollars: Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 both sit at 1.0 although their measured credit rates differ from their list ratio by more than twice, and moving one family's rows and not the others would put a second correction in the same field. What the assumption carries, measured on the rebuilt reports: of the 167 masterrig stretches recovered, the share of a stretch's meter dollars sitting on a weight-sensitive new model (Haiku, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 5.5) has median 0.0% and maximum 41.8%, and none is more than half; of jwork's 33, median 0.5% and maximum 2.6%; of dave's 22, median 0.9% but one stretch (2026-09-15, $2.82 of list value) is 100% Haiku and so entirely carried by the assumed weight. Opus 4.7 and 4.8 dominate several recovered masterrig stretches outright, up to 100%, and those carry no weight assumption at all because their list prices are Opus 5's.

_credits._source: Credits per token for the five-hour meter, as a REFERENCE TABLE only. The meter does not work in dollars: it charges ceil(input_tokens x input_rate + output_tokens x output_rate) of an internal unit, at a small rational rate per model. The per-family rates here are the Shellac reconstruction (https://she-llac.com/claude-limits, crossposted 2026-01-25), recorded with their derivation in docs/reference-2026-09-20-shellac-credits-model.md. That table is a January 2026 reference and never an input to arithmetic: the rates the page's per-model figures divide by are measured on the meter and live in history/model-rates.json (tools/model_rates.py, docs/findings-2026-09-20-measured-rates.md), which is where Sonnet's measured rate, Haiku's 'not measurable' and Fable's two disagreeing sides of 14 September come from. Two things here are still used: Opus's row, which is the unit anchor every measured rate is expressed against, and the cache-read weight, which is measured elsewhere (cache_read_weight_source) rather than taken from the article. The five-hour window and Fable's solved interval are measured in docs/findings-2026-09-20-reconciliation.md; Fable's interval is not stored here at all, it is solved from the stretches at publish time (reproduce with tools/reconcile_window.py over the watched accounts' stretch files). The dollar table above is untouched and still feeds the contributor path and the legacy token figures.
_credits.role_note: reference: shown beside a measurement, never used to state a per-model figure. The one exception is Opus's row, marked anchor below, which defines the unit -- and which nothing in our data tests, so if it is wrong every credit figure scales with it.
_credits.unit: credits per token. input and output are [numerator, denominator] so the exact fifteenths survive a JSON round trip; a consumer divides.
_credits.cache_write: charged at the model's plain input rate, not the API's 1.25x write premium
_credits.cache_read_weight_source: docs/findings-2026-09-20-reconciliation.md, 'Cache reads': at 0.015 the pure-Opus window reads 23.6M credits, above the 22M the May doubling implies; at 0 it reads 19.7M, between the two official-anchored figures. The data prefer a weight at or near zero; the 0 to 0.015 range from the fits is the uncertainty carried on every credit figure.

haiku.measured: not measurable from our stretches: see history/model-rates.json measured_rates.per_family.haiku. The highest Haiku share of any clean stretch on a fitted account is zero, so this row stands untested and the page publishes a status sentence rather than a number.

sonnet.measured: measured relative to Opus in history/model-rates.json measured_rates.per_family.sonnet, above this row's 6/15 in every fit. The page divides by the measured rate and draws this one beside it.

opus.note: every Opus version prices as Opus, which is why this table is keyed by family
opus.anchor_note: the unit anchor: what a credit means in this repository. Every other family's rate is measured relative to this row, and the fit rescales its Opus coefficient to it, so nothing in our data tests this row itself.

fable.interval_rule: computed at publish time by tracker/credits.py fable_interval, never stored here: the rate is solved per Fable-heavy stretch against the measured window, and the interval runs from the lowest per-account p25 at output 5x input to the highest per-account p25 at output 3x. Storing the endpoints would freeze a measurement into a table of reference rates, and it narrows as clean Fable-heavy stretches accrue from ordinary use.
fable.output_ratio_source: docs/reference-2026-09-20-shellac-credits-model.md: every model in the article's table uses output = 5x input; the same note fits 3 for Fable with a bootstrap interval of [3, 3]. docs/findings-2026-09-20-reconciliation.md: the output ratio (3x or 5x) is not separable from our stretches, so both candidates are carried and neither is chosen.
fable.interval_source: docs/findings-2026-09-20-reconciliation.md, "Fable's rate". Only three stretches on the account with a usable capture column survive the capture gate, and the solve is inflated wherever the meter counts machines the transcripts never saw, so both edges are a p25.
fable.measured: fitted on both sides of 2026-09-14 in history/model-rates.json measured_rates.per_family.fable, and the two sides do not agree within their intervals, so the page publishes the interval and the words 'rate not yet identified' rather than a rate.

_credits.list_price_model_note: which model id of the dollar table above prices a family's tokens in API dollars, where a family now has several rows (Opus 5, 5.5, 4.8 and 4.7; Sonnet 5 and 4.6) and they do not all list at the same price. It names the current model of the family, never the first row that happens to match. Haiku was null until 2026-09-23 because the family had no row in the dollar table at all; Claude Haiku 4.5 now has one, so the API value of a Haiku figure has a list price to use. Haiku's own credit rate is still not measurable from our stretches, so the published Haiku figures remain null with a status -- what changed is the reason the status gives.

across_cut_fable_rate.why: tools/reconcile_window.py section 3 holds this one rate on both sides of 2026-09-14 so the before and after medians can be compared with each other. It is not a claim about Fable's rate -- that is the interval above -- and it sits below the interval's low end; what makes the comparison work is that the same rate is in both medians.
